thread:
alex: heads up — we're getting a few support pages asking why users suddenly lose access when we change routing policies. can we discuss a UX for showing how permissions propagate across routes + model variants?

maria: thanks for surfacing. is this about tenant roles -> route scopes -> model-variant fallbacks? or something else?

alex: yes, exactly. e.g. tenant role grants `route:read` on `payments/*` but we have routing rules that rewrite `payments/legacy` to `payments/v2` and v2 uses a different service principal. people lose apparent access.

sam: that's nasty. two questions: how do we surface that in console, and how do we simulate changes before rolling out?

claire: from a design POV I think a compact "effective permissions" preview on each route row would help. hover or click -> modal showing: direct grants, inherited grants, routing rewrites, and fallback chains. minimal text, visual arrows.

jonah: security note: don't expose internal service principal names to tenants. show abstracted labels (e.g., "service: model-v2") and a link to audit logs for infra teams. also we need to record a deterministic path so audits match behavior.

maria: +1. product ask: add a "simulate as" action where admins can pick a role or user and click run to see allowed/denied for a route, including the routing policy effects.

alex: prototype idea: a panel that shows the evaluation graph. nodes: user -> role -> route pattern -> rewrite -> final model. edges annotated with grant/deny. color green/red.

sam: implementation thoughts: we already have an internal permissions-eval API used by backend. we could expose a read-only endpoint: `GET /internal/v1/eval?principal=...&path=/payments/legacy` that returns a flattened decision tree. example response shape (pseudo):
```
{
  "decision": "deny",
  "reasons": ["no direct grant on payments/legacy","route rewrite to payments/v2 requires model-v2 allow"]
}
```
Keep only the important fields.

claire: for console microcopy: "Effective permissions show who can call this route after routing and fallbacks are applied. Use 'simulate as' to preview changes before rollout." short.

jonah: telemetry: we should add a metric `rbac.simulate.count` and track simulate results (allowed/denied) and also `rbac.denied_after_rewrite` on production requests so we can spot regressions after policy changes. tag by org and route pattern.

maria: rollout UX: we need a canary toggle on policy changes that shows a simulated impact for X% of requests and collects denies. UI should surface projected affected principals and a small histogram of denied requests by role.

alex: edge case: what about deduping multiple routes that match a single request? the evaluation should show the chosen path and also other matching paths with reasons why they weren't selected.

sam: agree. backend will need to return `candidates` list with `score` and `picked: true|false` and `why_not` for others. keep it optional for heavy calls.

claire: UI idea: timeline scrubber in the modal to see "before" and "after" a policy change — show counts and sample principals.

jonah: privacy: when surfacing sample principals in the console ensure we redact PII and only show role ids or anonymized hashes unless org-admin permission.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new internal endpoint `GET /internal/v1/eval` added to infra backlog ticket INF-847.

maria: action items: 1) sam to spec API shape and opt-in `candidates` flag (due EOD Fri). 2) claire to mock modal with decision graph and simulate button (first pass Tue). 3) jonah to write threat/privacy checklist for sample principals (Mon). 4) alex to draft support KB wording.

alex: thanks all — this should cut down the noisy tickets. will sync in weekly eng-platform on Tuesday. :thumbsup:
